text:
Alex K.: quick follow-up from the RFC — thinking about the 'gpu reservoir' headroom idea. had a few concerns after sim runs.
Maria G.: nice, share the sims? high-level takeaways first pls.
Alex K.: baseline: reservoir keeps X GPUs warm for tail traffic. sim shows tenant fairness drifts when bursts overlap across tenants.
Cheng L.: do you mean one tenant's burst can starve others' credits? or they're just pushed to lower priority queues?
Alex K.: both. starvation sometimes happens because reservoir refills from same pool we use for steady traffic. refill timing aligns badly.
Priya S.: can we separate refill bandwidth from steady capacity? like a small dedicated accel pool that only feeds reservoir?
Devon: that adds infra cost. alternative: change admission to use token-buckets per-tenant + global soft-cap. that'd smooth but not eliminate worst-case SLA slips.
Alex K.: here's a sketch I pasted into sim as a toy:
```
policy {
  tenant_bucket(rate=R, burst=B)
  global_headroom(cap=H)
  reservoir_refill(rate=Rf) // capped per-cycle
  fallback: route->cheaper-model if wait>W
}
```
Maria G.: looks reasonable. curious about window sizes R vs Rf. any numbers from the sim?
Alex K.: used R=100tok/s, B=2s, H=4 GPUs, Rf=1 GPU/s. when 3 tenants burst simultaneously we saw two tenants hit 95th latency -> SLA alert.
Cheng L.: maybe add a priority decay: recent high-ratio bursters get temporary lower refill weight. gives fairness over minutes rather than seconds.
Priya S.: sounds like complexity for runtime state and edge cases on tenant churn. but doable. what's the cost of misclassification?
Devon: false positives mean we throttle a good tenant and push them to slower model -> soft revenue risk. false negatives mean SLA breach. need a clear tradeoff.
Alex K.: proposal: implement token-bucket + global_headroom + refill-rate limiter + priority-decay, start in canary for 10% traffic on dedicated pools. add per-tenant SLO guardrails to auto-escalate to reserved capacity if repeatedly throttled.
Maria G.: can we expose per-tenant refill stats in Console? teams will want visibility.
Alex K.: yes, add metrics: refill_rate, headroom_used, throttle_count, last_decay_reset.
Cheng L.: ops question: what happens on node failures while reservoir is mid-refill? do we instantly re-evaluate headroom?
Devon: autoscaler-bot: detected node failure -> drain initiated. recommended action: pause refill for 30s and recompute headroom based on live capacity.
autoscaler-bot: [info] simulated failover latency from our run: 12-18s to reach new steady allocation.
Priya S.: ok next steps: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with the policy DSL, decay rules, and canary plan. Alex, can you attach sim configs and graphs?
Alex K.: will upload sims + raw traces to the thread by EOD. thanks all. :thumbsup:
